clue.text: Poetic line one clad in Lycra mangled

indicators.note: clad in says the numeral is dressed in the scrambled fabric, wrapped by it
mangled says the letters of the fabric's name are knocked out of shape and rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone squeezed into a Lycra outfit that has been badly torn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mangled' turns LYCRA into LYRCA; 'clad in' puts I inside it, and L for line goes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyrical writing is expressive and song-like, which is the quality of poetry.

clue.text: Space for members the French prepare

parts.note: le is French for the
to groom is to prepare someone for a role

explanation.surface: French club members get a room ready.
explanation.definitionFit: Room to stretch one's legs, the limbs, in a car or plane.

clue.text: Queen enjoy sending up Independent writer

parts.note: R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

indicators.note: in a down entry, sending up moves a letter higher, nearer the top

parts.note: to like is to enjoy

explanation.surface: The Queen likes mocking a journalist from the Independent newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sending up' lifts the I of LIKE to its front, giving ILKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainer Maria Rilke was an Austrian poet, a writer.

clue.text: A blaze outside the tents affected passion

parts.note: camp means theatrically affected
fire means ardour, passion

explanation.surface: A fire around the tents stirs up showy emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Campers light one in the open air beside their tents for warmth.

clue.text: City taking possession of a new Turner?

indicators.note: taking possession of means holding, so the city goes round the other pieces

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A city acquires a new painting by Turner.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner suggests the painter; it is the Hollywood actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Lana Turner was a Hollywood film star, an example of someone surnamed so.

clue.text: In conversation, mock old man boobs

indicators.note: in conversation says the words are to be taken as spoken, by their sound

parts.note: faux, borrowed from French, means fake or mock; pa is an informal word for father, an old man

explanation.surface: Someone talking teases their dad about his blunders.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of the French phrase is silent, so FAUX PA said out loud matches it.
explanation.definitionFit: Boobs as a noun are blunders, and a social blunder is exactly this French phrase.

clue.text: Free love should carry a short warning

indicators.note: should carry places the warning first, carried on the front of the word for love
short says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: fore is the golfer's warning shout
love means nothing, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: Love that costs nothing ought to come with a brief caution.
explanation.definitionFit: Done without payment, gratis.

clue.text: Ill-advised popgun wiseguy's packing

indicators.note: packing means carrying inside, so the answer is concealed in the words

explanation.surface: A wiseguy carrying a toy gun is foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'packing' is gangster slang for carrying a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwise and ill-advised are synonyms for imprudent.

clue.text: Spooner says "wind up McCartney" — with this, perhaps

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the starting sounds of words

parts.note: to crank is to wind up a handle
Paul McCartney of the Beatles

explanation.surface: Someone wants to tease the former Beatle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind up' also means tease, which is what a hoax phone call does.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoax telephone call is a way to wind someone up.

clue.text: Sentry head of logistics treated harshly

indicators.note: treated means processed, so the letters are reworked
head of says to take the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A sentry is given rough treatment by a logistics chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Severely and strictly, as in a stern tone.

clue.text: Ring model about someone in a rush?

indicators.note: about, in the sense of moved around, says the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A jeweller's display piece for a ring is turned about.
explanation.walkthrough: The rush is a gold rush, not a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Prospectors joined the gold rushes of California and the Klondike to dig for the precious metal.

clue.text: Weight? Well, I'm a big-boned beast!

parts.note: hale means healthy, well

explanation.surface: Someone defends their weight by claiming to be big-boned.
explanation.definitionFit: The great sea mammal is the largest animal there is, skeleton included.

clue.text: A certain aside never to be repeated

parts.note: one can mean a certain, as in 'one Mr Smith'
off means to one side, aside

explanation.surface: A particular remark made in passing that must not be said again.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening only once is unique and will not recur.

clue.text: Abandoned on account of rice wine? Not initially

parts.note: for can mean because of, on account of
sake is Japanese rice wine

indicators.note: initially says to take only the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A drinker gives something up because of Japanese wine, though not at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not initially' looks like an instruction to drop a first letter; it supplies the N of 'Not'.
explanation.definitionFit: Forsaken describes someone deserted or left behind, the same as abandoned.

clue.text: 24hrs in which Bob is all over the place?

definitions.text: 24hrs in which Bob is all over the place?

parts.words: 24hrs in which Bob is all over the place
parts.note: a bob is a haircut, so a day when it is messy

explanation.surface: A day when someone called Bob is chaotic.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob looks like a name; it is the short hairstyle.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names any day of frustration, when nothing goes right.

clue.text: One seen cruising room with chatty cast

indicators.note: cast, as in cast about or thrown, signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A theatre room full of a talkative cast of actors.
explanation.definitionFit: A powered pleasure boat is something you would see cruising along a coast.

clue.text: Con hunter twirling this?

indicators.note: twirling means spinning round, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A police officer chasing criminals spins a baton.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer's baton is something a constable might twirl while hunting crooks.

clue.text: Darling times entertaining a bishop

indicators.note: entertaining means holding a guest, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: by means times in multiplication, as in two by three
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A sweetheart repeatedly plays host to a churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: Baby is a common term of endearment, like darling or sweetheart.

clue.text: Want wordplay that leads the solver to silver?

definitions.text: wordplay that leads the solver to silver?
definitions.meaning: a clue writing 'short' for the symbol Ag leads to silver; split as short Ag, then e

explanation.surface: A clue that leads its solver to silver.
explanation.definitionFit: Want means a lack or insufficiency of something.

clue.text: Take breath away by giving two veg a twist

indicators.note: giving joins with 'a twist' to signal the word is turned round
a twist turns the word round so it reads backwards

parts.note: nuts, plural for the two, are loosely counted among vegetable foods

explanation.surface: A cook astonishes diners by twisting a pair of vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to astound, the effect of something breathtaking.

clue.text: Faceless corporation behind small-town firm

indicators.note: behind puts the belly after the other pieces

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for town

indicators.note: faceless says the first letter is removed

parts.note: corporation is an old jokey word for a pot belly

explanation.surface: An anonymous corporation backs a small-town firm.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse lists pieces in answer order: S, T, then AUNCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Staunch means steadfast, loyal and unwavering.

clue.text: Animal picking up icepack for jaw-leading boxer?

indicators.note: picking up means hearing, so the phrase is taken by its sound

parts.note: a fighter who leads with his chin would need something to cool it: a chin chiller

explanation.surface: A boxer who leads with his jaw needs an icepack afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: A boxer who 'leads with his chin' takes many punches there.
explanation.definitionFit: This soft-furred South American rodent is a kind of animal.

clue.text: Menial labours beginning in the cold?

indicators.note: labours means struggles, so the letters toss about
beginning in says to take the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Servants toil in cold weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold is an example of a minor illness.

clue.text: Baptist regularly drinking rum in conflict

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so one piece goes inside
regularly says to take every other letter

parts.note: rum means odd, strange

explanation.surface: A Baptist often drinks rum, which is at odds with faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at odds is being in disagreement.

clue.text: A little bounder in a cravat

parts.note: a Scottie, the Scottish terrier, is a small dog that bounds about

explanation.surface: A small cad wearing a neck scarf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounder' suggests a cad; here it is a dog that bounds.
explanation.definitionFit: This wide neckcloth is named after Royal Ascot races, a formal cravat.

clue.text: A jolly female you left close to a pint for Tony?

parts.note: a Jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM
U is text-speak for you

explanation.surface: A cheerful woman leaves near a pint of beer meant for Tony.
explanation.walkthrough: In Tony Hancock's sketch The Blood Donor, he is horrified that a pint is 'very nearly an armful'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hancock's famous line equates a pint of donated blood to roughly a limb's fill.

clue.text: Celebrity cuddling large lover

indicators.note: cuddling means embracing, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: fame means celebrity

explanation.surface: A celebrity hugs their big partner.
explanation.definitionFit: An old flame is a former sweetheart.

clue.text: Perhaps a key passage missing its introduction

indicators.note: missing its introduction says the first letter goes

parts.note: an aisle is a passage

explanation.surface: A musical passage lacking an introduction is in a key.
explanation.walkthrough: A key is a low island, as in the Florida Keys.
explanation.definitionFit: A key, or cay, is an example of a small island.

clue.text: Gut-churning gas, heading to dunny a lot

indicators.note: churning says the letters are stirred up and rearranged

parts.note: neon is a noble gas

indicators.note: heading to says to take the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A nauseating smell sends someone hurrying to the toilet repeatedly.
explanation.walkthrough: A dunny is Australian slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means endlessly, in abundance, as in 'it cost no end'.

clue.text: Different insult, standard answer: t***e*!

parts.note: to dis is to insult
par is the standard, as in up to par
the starred-out word leaves only the letters T and E showing

explanation.surface: An unusual insult, with a censored swear word as the standard reply.
explanation.walkthrough: The asterisks hide letters, so the word supplies just its visible T and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Disparate things are fundamentally unlike one another, distinct in kind.

clue.text: Really striking Liberal integrity

indicators.note: striking means striking out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: honestly can mean really, as an intensifier

explanation.surface: A truly impressive Liberal politician known for being principled.
explanation.definitionFit: Integrity is the quality of being truthful and upright.

clue.text: He's one to detail meteorological forces

indicators.note: to detail is read as de-tail, removing the last letter

parts.note: the elements are wind, rain and weather

explanation.surface: A forecaster who sets out the weather in detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' is the chemical symbol for helium, not a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Helium, symbol He, is one of the chemical substances in the periodic table.
